text: Four days later, the bell for the next race
why: ¶214 says 'there goes the bell', and ¶156-157 show the 'four days later' train trip to Winchester for the race.

text: How are the trainer's murder and the favourite's disappearance connected? — the horse killed the trainer, who was harming it, and then ran loose
id: q.connection=the horse killed the trainer, who was harming it, and then ran loose
why: The 'ran loose' part conflicts with the story so far: ¶204 says Holmes found the horse in a faker's hands, and ¶214 names the horse as the killer, not a loose animal. The claim that the trainer was harming the horse is also not stated.

text: In what way was John Straker unworthy of the Colonel's confidence?
why: ¶214 says Straker was 'entirely unworthy of your confidence', so the question follows from the story and does not point to a particular answer.

text: In what way was John Straker unworthy of the Colonel's confidence? — he meant to lame the favourite himself
id: q.straker_unworthy=he meant to lame the favourite himself
why: Nothing so far suggests Straker planned to harm or lame the horse. Lameness appears only in the sheep (¶173), and Straker is described as zealous and honest (¶19, ¶75).

text: In what way was John Straker unworthy of the Colonel's confidence? — he kept a costly second life under the name of Derbyshire
id: q.straker_unworthy=he kept a costly second life under the name of Derbyshire
why: The milliner's bill to 'William Derbyshire', a friend whose letters went to Straker's house, and Holmes's remark on 'Madam Derbyshire's expensive tastes' (¶84-85), give the reader reason to consider a hidden second life. The story has not confirmed it.

text: In what way was John Straker unworthy of the Colonel's confidence? — he had money on the race against his own horse
id: q.straker_unworthy=he had money on the race against his own horse
why: The story has built up heavy betting on the race (Simpson's book, Brown's large bets, the favourite's odds), so a trainer betting against his own horse is a possibility the reader has reason to consider. It is not confirmed.
